sections.content: How many people stayed in Downham Market after gaining qualifications?

Downham Market is a small town in the East of England. Downham Market does not have its own university.

Downham Market has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Downham Market ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 365 state-school pupils from Downham Market who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 95 (26%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 110 (30%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Downham Market to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Downham Market's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Downham Market in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Downham Market move to?

Of Downham Market's graduates, 55 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

Of Downham Market's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 55 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 25 of those qualified non-graduates (45%) were living fairly locally, in the King's Lynn travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Downham Market's GCSE cohort:

  • 35 graduates left the East of England

In 2018 to 2019, 53% of graduates and 56% of qualified non-graduates living in Downham Market had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 85 graduates and 125 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Downham Market. This is compared with the 95 graduates and 110 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 41% of the graduates had also lived in Downham Market as GCSE pupils, while 53% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Downham Market in 2018 to 2019, 44% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 56% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
